short: I think my phone has a virus
title: I think my phone has a virus: what you can do now
pageTitle: I think my phone has a virus: what you can do now | Spamlock
description: Pop-ups, apps you didn’t install or a slow phone? Steps you can take now: don’t tap the pop-up, remove apps you don’t know, run a scan, update, and reset if it keeps happening.
answer: Don’t tap pop-ups that say your phone is infected. Delete apps you don’t recognise, update the phone, and on Android run a Play Protect scan. If problems keep coming back, you can reset the phone.
stepsTitle: Steps you can take if you think your phone has a virus

steps.title: Don’t tap the pop-up
steps.text: Pop-ups that say your phone is infected often pretend to be Apple or another company. Close the browser tab instead, and if a pop-up tells you to call a number, don’t call it.

steps.title: Not confident? Get help
steps.text: From your phone maker’s support, a phone shop you trust, or someone you know who’s good with phones. Never from someone who calls or messages you first offering to fix it.

steps.title: Delete apps you don’t recognise
steps.text: Look for apps you didn’t install or don’t use, and delete them. If your iPhone says an app contains malware, tap Delete App on the alert.

steps.title: Android: run a Play Protect scan
steps.text: Play Protect is built into Android phones with Google Play. It checks your apps for harmful ones and can remove them.

steps.title: Update the phone
steps.text: In Settings, look for Software Update. Updates fix security holes.

steps.title: Still happening? Reset the phone
steps.text: The UK’s cyber security centre recommends a factory reset for a phone, because antivirus apps usually can’t clean phones the way they clean computers. A reset erases everything, so back up your photos and contacts first.
